projects.name: Unveiling the Influence of Amplifying Language-Specific Neurons
projects.description: This research titled 'Unveiling the Influence of Amplifying Language-Specific Neurons' has been accepted to AACL 2025. It studies the amplification of language-specific neurons in large language models (LLMs). It involves identifying and intervening language-specific neurons in several autoregressive models, with the purpose of model interpretability.

projects.name: Sparse Autoencoders Can Capture Language-Specific Concepts Across Diverse Languages
projects.description: This research titled 'Sparse Autoencoders Can Capture Language-Specific Concepts Across Diverse Languages' studies how sparse autoencoders (SAEs) can find monosemantic, language-specific features inside large language models (LLMs). It introduces SAE-LAPE, a method based on feature activation probability, to identify language-specific features within the feed-forward network. These features mostly appear in the middle-to-final layers, are interpretable, influence the model's multilingual performance and output language, and can be used for language identification with performance comparable to fastText, with the purpose of model interpretability.
